Welcome to King Solomon Academy
Welcome to King Solomon Academy. Our school is defined by our mission to provide all pupils who attend KSA with the choice at 18 years of age to attend a selective university and be able to be happy and successful in their lives.
Nursery • Primary • Secondary • Sixth form
Year 7 Oxford Residential
Bronze Duke of Edinburgh’s Award qualifier
Summit Celebration 2026
Admissions
Explore what makes our Academy great, how to apply, and when our open days are.
Get a place
Parent hub
All the information our parents need to know in one handy place.

King Solomon Academy Sixth Form Open Evening 7th October 5-6pm, all applicants welcome!Sixth Form Applications are open!
Nursery
Our provision
Our Nursery offers provision from when a child turns 2 years of age until they enter Reception in the September after they turn 4 years of age.
For 2 year olds we offer paid places (full days, mornings or afternoons) and Local Authority funded places (mornings or afternoons, top up options available). For 3 and 4 year olds, places are full day and free of charge (8.20 - 3pm).
Exceptional Nursery provision
We have invested significantly in ensuring our Nursery children get the very best start to life at KSA.
The building is purpose built as our nursery, co-designed with Early Years specialists to ensure it is the most enabling environment for our primary users: your children! Every decision about every piece of furniture, every peg and every light switch was made with your children in mind. We invested in high quality Community Playthings resources and furnishings, so the environment is inspiring, comfortable and safe.
Children free flow every day into our extra-ordinary outdoor learning environment. Designed by our team and Early Years experts, we created an amazing space for children to exercise and learn across all seventeen learning areas and develop their independence, imagination and self-confidence. Children have access to a woodland space with a tree house, sand pits, sensory and mud kitchens, climbing frames, water features and even a performance area.
Age 2+ provision
We opened our provision for 2-year-olds in September 2021. We are delighted to seize the opportunity to build relationships with our families from such a young age, building the foundations that will help our pupils to be happy and nurtured in the nursery years.
Our 2-year-old provision:
The timings of the day are set up so that siblings can conveniently attend the 3-year-old and primary school day. Pupils who attend the 2-year-old nursery retain their nursery place when they become 3 years old, when full time (8.30-3pm provision) is available - without cost - to all families.
Age 3+ provision
Our Nursery environment is characterised by the formation of extremely positive and influential relationships between the school, pupils and their parents. We aim to support the development of the whole child, including their upbringing at home. Our curriculum is rich and varied teachers are encouraged to dream big in their curriculum choices to inspire and engage pupils.
Our 3-year-old provision:
Rise Reception Network
RISE Reception Networks: King Solomon Academy is a Lead School
The RISE Reception Networks bring together Reception practitioners and leaders to strengthen early years practice through collaboration, reflection and shared learning.
The Department for Education have set a target of 75% children to reach a Good Level of Development by 2028.
As a Lead School, King Solomon Academy coordinates opportunities for schools to connect, explore effective Reception practice and support continuous improvement.
Which Lead School?
We are one of five Lead Schools across Greater London. Below you can find which boroughs each Lead School support:
Ark King Solomon Academy:
Brent, Camden, Ealing, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hammersmith & Fulham, Hounslow, Kensington & Chelsea, Kingston upon Thames, Richmond upon Thames, Westminster, City of London
Charles Dickens Primary and Nursery School:
Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham, Southwark, Wandsworth
Davies Lane Primary School:
Barnet, Enfield, Redbridge, Waltham Forest, Haringey
Tollgate Primary School:
Barking & Dagenham, Hackney, Havering, Islington, Newham, Tower Hamlets
Rockmount Primary School:
Bexley, Bromley, Croydon, Merton, Sutton,
What more can I learn?
This webpage provides a central access point for resources, examples and links that support Reception improvement and complement the work of the RISE Reception Networks.
The networks are intended to act as a supportive professional community where schools can:
Share and reflect on evidence‑informed Reception practice
Get involved!
Schools involved in the RISE Reception Networks benefit from:
Who Can Take Part?
The RISE Reception Networks are open to:
Schools can join at any point and engage in ways that best suit their context and priorities.
Reception class teachers
Early Years leaders
To join our network fill in the online form
Want to learn more? Here are some links for further reading:

King Solomon Academy Sixth Form Open Evening 7th October 5-6pm, all applicants welcome!Sixth Form Applications are open!
Welcome to King Solomon Academy Sixth Form
King Solomon Academy is one of the best Sixth Form choices in London. Our school exists to ensure every single one of our students is able to achieve the highest possible academic outcomes and go on to study at the best universities in the UK and beyond, or on a degree level apprenticeship of their choice.
Located in the heart of central London, right next to Edgware Road tube station and a few minutes’ walk from bustling Oxford Street, KSA is a truly metropolitan Sixth Form. Our Sixth Form is the final step in our all-through school journey. Some of our students have been with us since they were two years old in Nursery but we are always delighted to receive strong applications from highly motivated and ambitious students from a range of backgrounds. We have pupils joining us from across London, and Internationally too.
KSA is a small school, where we know each and every student extremely well. Our teachers are exceptional graduates from the best universities in the world, achieving extraordinary outcomes in their subjects for our students and supporting them to enjoy a wide range of extra-curricular activities, university visits and residential trips to Bath University in Year 12 and Berlin in Year 13. We have a mantra about doing whatever it takes to secure success for every single one of our students.
KSA Sixth Form Leadership Team 2026-2027
How to apply
Applications are made directly to our sixth form via the link below.
Each student must complete an application form with details of predicted grades and related course options. We then send out conditional offers based on the student’s predicted grades and their related courses options at that time. Offers are subject to change in accordance with the actual results a student achieves.
If you have any questions about the admissions process, don't hesitate to get in contact via sixthform@kingsolomonacademy.org
Subjects
Our Sixth Form offer includes a wide range of A-Levels, and BTEC Extended Diploma in Business.
Most pupils are expected to take three courses with BTEC extended diploma counting as the equivalent of three A levels. As A levels have moved to linear assessment and university offers are for three subjects, students are encouraged to focus on excelling in three subjects from the start. Each course is taught over six, fifty five minute lessons each. Pupils are expected to at least match those hours in independent study.
Some pupils also choose to study for additional qualifications, such as the EPQ.
In the video below, you can hear more from some KSA alumni on results day about their subject choices and their next steps.
We offer the following courses at A Level. Click each subject link to find out more about this subject at King Solomon Academy.
Students follow courses that last for two years. At the end of Year 1 there will be internal examinations in A level subjects. These exams will determine students’ suitability to continue into Year 13 and will also be used to produce predicted grades to be sent to universities. BTEC students will sit two external examinations in Year 12 that do count towards their final grade – both exams must be passed for students to receive their qualification. All external exams for A level subjects will happen at the end of the second year of study and make up 100% of the final grade (except for History, English and Geography which have a coursework element). BTEC students will sit another two external exams in Year 13 alongside their coursework units.
Pathways
We offer two key pathways at Ark King Solomon Sixth Form.
We offer the core academic A Level subjects that we know are most valued by good universities, and that allow you to keep your progression options as open as possible. Most students will study three linear A levels; some will take a fourth subject, depending on GCSE results.
Entry criteria: 5 Grade 6s and above in GSCEs, including English and Maths (not including BTECs or other equivalents). You will also need to meet the individual entry criteria for specific subjects.
Explore our subjects
Our two BTEC options, Business (Level 3) and Applied Science (Level 3) are part of the Ark Professional Pathways programme. These courses expose our students to real world experiences, enabling them to go on to be successful on their chosen pathway, be that a top third university or a degree apprenticeship.
Entry criteria: 5 Grade 5s and above in GSCEs, including English and Maths (not including BTECs or other equivalents).
Open days
KSA Sixth Form Open Evenings will be on - Wednesday 7th October 2026 5-6pm Tuesday 12th January 2027 5-6pm
Please complete the form below to sign up.
Ark's unique Professional Pathways programme
Sixth formers love our unique vocational alternative to A levels, which provides them with the skills they need to thrive at university and throughout their career.
Access game-changing bursaries
For Year 13 leavers going onto higher education, we offer bursaries ranging from £3,000 to £50,000 to help with the financial costs of university life.
Best-in-class careers provision
Our pupils dream big for life after school thanks to our highly aspirational careers programme, which includes visits to prestigious universities and employers, one-to-one guidance and a rich programme of workshops and visiting speakers.

King Solomon Academy Sixth Form Open Evening 7th October 5-6pm, all applicants welcome!Sixth Form Applications are open!
Welcome to King Solomon Academy
Welcome to King Solomon Academy. Our school is defined by our mission to provide a rigorous and transformational education to every pupil enabling them to have the choice to go on to a top university at 18 and preparing them to lead happy and successful lives.
Our school is a community of staff, parents and pupils aligned around a shared belief that every child must receive an excellent education, that every child can and will feel safe, happy and successful in our school and in their lives beyond. We are a team and family living by our values to aim high, work together, be kind and lead the way.
We are one school with two sites. Our Younger Years Site is a beautiful space, tucked away at the bottom of Crompton Street. Our new state of the art nursery building and beautiful outdoor environment serve our 2-4 year olds. 90 children in each cohort in Reception to Year 4 play in our extensive outdoor areas including a woodland garden and Forest School provision. Pupils move to our Older Years Site on Penfold Street for Year 5-Year 13 benefitting from our large Sports Hall, MUGA, specialist science facilities and specialist music provision. Every pupil at King Solomon plays a strings instrument from Year 4 to Year 9, playing together in a year group orchestra throughout Middle School.
We hope you enjoy reading more about the academy and I look forward to meeting you.
Beth Humphreys
Climbing the mountain to university
Our mission is to provide our pupils with a rigorous and transformational education which prepares them for success at university and beyond. We ensure that every pupil achieves academic success, particularly in reading, writing and maths where we ensure every child learns with confidence.
We want to make university education accessible, exciting and aspirational. Our pupils work hard towards this goal because we make it real for them. We name our classes after university cities and we name each year group by the year in which they will graduate from sixth form. We run annual residential trips from Year 5 up for every pupil, investing in learning beyond the confines of our classrooms, having fun together and experiencing future opportunities open to us all. In Year 6, we spend a week in Oxford and whilst we love our day of outward bounds activities, we also love the days at the university attending a chemistry lecture, playing university sports and going punting on the river.
At the heart of our approach is that we are an all-through school with a thriving nursery provision. We believe in investing in knowing our pupils and their families extremely well, and we prioritise our pupils making extraordinary progress in the early years of their education. This sense of continued long-term commitment to each and every year of a child’s education is core to our approach.
We have high expectations for all of our pupils and believe that with great teaching and a lot of love and care, every child here can fulfil their potential. Our warm/strict approach means pupils feel safe and secure in the school but also confident to contribute to the future of the school and their community.
Long term, we commit to playing our part in removing the educational disadvantage currently experienced by those born into deprivation in our country. We strive to create role models and leaders in our community and through them create a safer, fairer, and happier society.
How we deliver a world-class education
High expectations - We are all climbing the mountain to university and are ambitious for every pupil.
Excellent teaching - We love teaching and we love learning, and we place it at the heart of all our work.
A rigorous and transformational curriculum - Our all-through curriculum is meticulously designed and implemented to ensure that our pupils have a successful journey from nursery through to university.
Exemplary character - Our school culture leads our pupils to be striving to be the best versions of ourselves. Our Personal Development curriculum invests in each pupil as an individual ensuring they are building the knowledge and skills to keep themselves and others safe, mentally and physically healthy and well informed about the world they live in.
A long-term commitment to every pupil - As one of a handful of all-through schools with consistent cohorts of children across primary and secondary, we are able to invest in our pupils and their families over the long-term, building deep and trusting relationships leading to sustainable and meaningful change.
Investment in our team - Our staff choose to work at KSA because we know we are working together to address educational inequality, and are well supported to achieve this.
Efficient and effective organisation - We carefully organise the operational and educational activities in our school to maximise our collective impact and make our work sustainable.
Our core values are woven throughout school life
Culture and wellbeing

As A levels have moved to linear assessment and university offers are for three subjects, students are encouraged to focus on excelling in three subjects from the start. Each course is taught over six, fifty five minute lessons each. Pupils are expected to at least match those hours in independent study.
Some pupils also choose to study for additional qualifications, such as the EPQ.
In the video below, you can hear more from some KSA alumni on results day about their subject choices and their next steps.
We offer the following courses at A Level. Click each subject link to find out more about this subject at King Solomon Academy.
Students follow courses that last for two years. At the end of Year 1 there will be internal examinations in A level subjects. These exams will determine students’ suitability to continue into Year 13 and will also be used to produce predicted grades to be sent to universities. BTEC students will sit two external examinations in Year 12 that do count towards their final grade – both exams must be passed for students to receive their qualification. All external exams for A level subjects will happen at the end of the second year of study and make up 100% of the final grade (except for History, English and Geography which have a coursework element). BTEC students will sit another two external exams in Year 13 alongside their coursework units.
Pathways
We offer two key pathways at Ark King Solomon Sixth Form.
We offer the core academic A Level subjects that we know are most valued by good universities, and that allow you to keep your progression options as open as possible. Most students will study three linear A levels; some will take a fourth subject, depending on GCSE results.
Entry criteria: 5 Grade 6s and above in GSCEs, including English and Maths (not including BTECs or other equivalents). You will also need to meet the individual entry criteria for specific subjects.
Explore our subjects
Our two BTEC options, Business (Level 3) and Applied Science (Level 3) are part of the Ark Professional Pathways programme. These courses expose our students to real world experiences, enabling them to go on to be successful on their chosen pathway, be that a top third university or a degree apprenticeship.
Entry criteria: 5 Grade 5s and above in GSCEs, including English and Maths (not including BTECs or other equivalents).
Open days

Ark's unique Professional Pathways programme
Sixth formers love our unique vocational alternative to A levels, which provides them with the skills they need to thrive at university and throughout their career.
Access game-changing bursaries
For Year 13 leavers going onto higher education, we offer bursaries ranging from £3,000 to £50,000 to help with the financial costs of university life.
Best-in-class careers provision
Our pupils dream big for life after school thanks to our highly aspirational careers programme, which includes visits to prestigious universities and employers, one-to-one guidance and a rich programme of workshops and visiting speakers.
